article.headline: Hamilton rain washout forces Black Caps into desperate fight for series draw
article.summary: Heavy rain at Seddon Park abandoned the third ODI between New Zealand and India, leaving the hosts trailing 2-0 in the series.
article.body:
Not a single ball was bowled in Hamilton as persistent weather forced officials to abandon the third ODI of the series. The washout effectively ended New Zealand’s hopes of an ODI series victory against India, leaving the Black Caps unable to win the remaining two matches after already falling 2-0 behind following losses in Auckland and Wellington. The team now faces the prospect of their first home ODI series defeat since 2019.

This result is significant for the Black Caps, who have successfully defended their home turf by winning 11 consecutive ODI series over the last five years. For local fans who turned out for the sellout event, the abandonment denied any chance of a 40-overs-per-side contest. The loss of points and momentum comes at a difficult time as the squad prepares for upcoming test matches.

The challenge for New Zealand deepens as they enter games four and five without several key starters. Players including Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Henry Nicholls, and Nathan Smith are set to depart the ODI group to begin preparations for the test series in Wellington. Additionally, the side faces setbacks with players like Lockie Ferguson withdrawn due to injury, requiring a roster shuffle that brings in reinforcements like Finn Allen and Nick Kelly.

With only two games remaining, New Zealand must secure wins at Bay Oval to avoid a series loss. Both upcoming fixtures will test the depth of the squad as they look to salvage a 2-2 draw.

article.headline: Public Sector Strike Looms As Fifty Thousand Workers Prepare For Nationwide Rallies
article.summary: Irish public sector unions are weighing a revised pay offer while maintaining strike plans for Thursday as negotiations continue at the Workplace Relations Commission.
article.body:
While 50,000 workers prepare for nationwide rallies this Thursday, the Government and unions remain locked in high-stakes negotiations to avert a second all-out public sector strike in as many months. More than 20,000 people are expected to participate in the Dublin demonstration alone, according to the Irish Examiner. Union sources emphasize that plans for the industrial action remain in place, with Fórsa deputy general secretary Katie Morgan confirming that preparations must continue until an agreement is formally established. 

Resolving the pay dispute is critical for the Government, as the planned stoppage coincides with the European Political Community summit in Dublin, an event expected to host approximately 50 European leaders. A senior government source acknowledged that while a narrow window remains to reach a deal, the situation is urgent, noting that failing to secure an agreement by Wednesday morning could make it too late to prevent the strike. 

According to RTÉ, the current proposal under consideration by unions involves a 10.75% pay increase over two years and nine months, extending through March 2029. The Irish Examiner reports that an alternative revised offer includes a 10.5% increase, with lower-paid workers potentially receiving up to 17.8% in improvements, alongside an additional backdated payment for 2026 of €1,200 or 2%, whichever is greater. 

Taoiseach Micheál Martin has stated he believes the basis for strike action no longer exists, citing a constructive atmosphere in current talks. Meanwhile, Fórsa General Secretary Kevin Callinan has expressed a commitment to reaching a deal, though he noted that success depends entirely on the speed and outcome of the ongoing mediation process at the Workplace Relations Commission.
